items = List([t1, t2, t3, t4], "bullet")

t1 = ListItem("Dispatchability is the real currency", "Hydro is the only one of the three that can be told to produce more, now. Solar and wind follow the weather, so a town on them alone needs storage or a grid import.")
t2 = ListItem("Hydro's fuel is rain", "A dry season is a brownout, and the same water is wanted for irrigation and drinking. That is a political constraint, not a technical one, and it must be settled before design.")
t3 = ListItem("Wind's danger is a plausible site", "A regional wind map is not a site measurement. A turbine put on a mediocre hill is the most expensive mistake in this comparison, because it is invisible until the first full year of data.")
t4 = ListItem("Cost shape differs more than cost", "Solar and wind front-load nothing but build cost and have no fuel bill. Hydro is expensive to build and then cheap for fifty years, which rewards a town that can finance it and keep it maintained.")

c48f23922681.text:
// jarvis-context: W10=
root = Col([head, cards, loadSection, closing], 20)

head = Col([Title("What holds a suspension bridge up", "2xl"), Caption("The deck is not the strong part. It is handed to cables, and the cables are handed to the ground.")], 4)

cards = Carousel([card1, card2, card3], 320, 16)

card1 = Card([SearchImage("Golden Gate Bridge San Francisco", 1.5, 10), Title("Golden Gate Bridge", "md"), Caption("San Francisco, 1937 · main span 1,280 m"), Text("Steel towers 227 m above the water, two cables with 27,572 wires each, deck hung from 250 pairs of vertical suspenders.")], "outline", 12, 8)

card2 = Card([SearchImage("Brooklyn Bridge New York", 1.5, 10), Title("Brooklyn Bridge", "md"), Caption("New York, 1883 · main span 486 m"), Text("Stone and granite towers; the deck is carried partly by main cables and partly by the diagonal stays spreading from each tower, a hybrid the Roeblings insisted on.")], "outline", 12, 8)

card3 = Card([SearchImage("Akashi Kaikyo Bridge Japan", 1.5, 10), Title("Akashi Kaikyō Bridge", "md"), Caption("Kobe–Awaji, 1998 · main span 1,991 m"), Text("The longest suspension span in the world. Its towers stand in one of the deepest, fastest tidal straits, and its two cables hold a deck of roughly 4,000 m between anchorages.")], "outline", 12, 8)

loadSection = Col([Title("The chain of load", "lg"), Text("Follow one piece of asphalt upward and you pass through five links. Nothing else holds it."), items], 10)

items = List([stepTower, stepCable, stepSuspenders, stepAnchorage, stepDeck, stepStiffness], "number")

stepTower = ListItem("Gravity and compression — towers", "Load arrives down the cable, bends over the tower saddle and comes out again on the other side. The two vertical pulls nearly cancel, so the tower mostly feels compression, straight down into its pier and the riverbed.")
stepCable = ListItem("Tension — the main cable", "The main cable hangs in a catenary and is asked to do the hardest job on the bridge: resist being pulled apart. It is the only member spanning from one end of the bridge to the other, and it works in pure tension, which steel is superb at.")
stepSuspenders = ListItem("Vertical hangers", "Short cables or rods drop from the main cable to the deck at close intervals. They lift the deck, so the main cable's load stays smooth: the whole deck becomes a rope-hung curtain rather than a beam.")
stepAnchorage = ListItem("Mass — the anchorages", "At each end the main cable runs into a block of concrete or rock. The cable is pulling that block toward the river; the block's own mass and its grip on bedrock simply refuse to move. The bridge is only as firm as the ground it is tied into.")
stepDeck = ListItem("Stiffness — the truss or box girder", "A flexible deck would ripple in the wind and hog under traffic. The deck is made a stiffened beam or truss so moving load on one section shares into the cable at neighbouring hangers. It does not carry the span; it keeps the span behaving.")
stepStiffness = ListItem("Balance — the spectrum, not the parts", "Every span has modes it loves to sway in. Bridges are tuned so wind pushes them off those frequencies; the Akashi Kaikyō's deck was reshaped after wind-tunnel testing of a full model, and the Golden Gate's famous orange paint is a corrosion defence as much as a livery.")

closing = Card([Title("In one line", "sm"), Text("The cable pulls, the tower is pushed, the anchorage hangs on to the ground — and everything between them is only there to hand movement upward to the cable.")], "soft", 14, 6)

4c00ab5c0764.text:
-- ANSI SQL: returns one row with NULL when there is no second-highest value
SELECT MAX(salary) AS second_highest_salary
FROM   Employee
WHERE  salary < (SELECT MAX(salary) FROM Employee);

-- Window-function version, if you also want it to work per department
-- or to see ties explicitly:
SELECT salary AS second_highest_salary
FROM (
    SELECT salary,
           DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY salary DESC) AS rnk
    FROM   Employee
) ranked
WHERE rnk = 2;
